rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent stepped/cascading mass in all four views, so gesture clarity and silhouette resolution are decent. However, the visible mass is mostly a compact rectangular prism with repeated roof ribs and no strong public void, entry seam, or ground-level opening responding to the verified access edge; the blue frontage is effectively ignored. That makes it underperform for neighborhood living, whose semantic contract asks for an active street threshold and one legible public court/terrace. The section also feels more like a compact roofed object than a clearly occupied mixed-use street building with public ground logic. It is repairable, but not program-fit as shown.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked massing with a clear primary datum and stepped upper articulation can support mixed-use hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More inward and enclosed than the candidate; less useful for the access-edge response.
